message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic chills and modern scares you might enjoy for a Friday‑night movie marathon:

| # | Title | Year | Why It’s Worth Watching |
|---|-------|------|--------------------------|
| 1 | **The Shining** (1980) | A psychological thriller set in an isolated hotel, featuring Jack Nicholson’s iconic descent into madness. |
| 2 | **Get Out** (2017) | A smart social satire wrapped in a horror package, blending dread with sharp commentary on race. |
| 3 | **Hereditary** (2018) | A family drama that turns into a relentless nightmare; the atmosphere is suffocatingly tense. |
| 4 | **A Quiet Place** (2018) | Silence is survival—watch how sound design becomes a character in its own right. |
| 5 | **Midsommar** (2019) | A daylight horror that subverts expectations, with unsettling folk rituals and gorgeous cinematography. |
| 6 | **It Follows** (2014) | An inventive premise where a curse is transmitted through sexual encounters; the creeping dread is palpable. |
| 7 | **The Conjuring** (2013) | A grounded supernatural tale based on real-life paranormal investigators Ed & Lorraine Warren. |
| 8 | **The Babadook** (2014) | A psychological horror about grief and motherhood, with a truly terrifying monster. |
| 9 | **Suspiria** (1977) | Dario Argento’s color‑splashed ballet of blood and intrigue—a cult favorite. |
|10 | **The Cabin in the Woods** (2012) | A meta‑take on the genre that starts as a cliché but ends up being a clever twist. |

Feel free to shuffle them or pick a theme—whether it’s supernatural, psychological, or slasher—and enjoy your fright-filled Friday!
